text:
A catheter valve is unsuitable when the bladder cannot safely store urine, including limited capacity, detrusor overactivity, ureteric reflux, renal impairment, or no filling sensation. It is also unsuitable when the person or a carer cannot open it reliably every few hours because of cognitive impairment or poor manual dexterity, and after recent bladder or urethral surgery that needs continuous free drainage. Those patients need continuous drainage into a bag; patient preference and not needing to measure urine are reasons a valve may be appropriate, not reasons to avoid one.

CONFIDENCE: 86
